design.rationale: Accuracy: the protocol composition (POST SSE terminating at the single final response, GET SSE for server notifications, Last-Event-ID distinct from the application journal cursor, resources/subscribe on the exact URI, resources/updated carrying the URI, progress ending with the request, no custom standard methods, honest pagination and list_changed caveats) matches the supplied MCP rules, and the Android facts checked (foreground service types, Android 15 BOOT_COMPLETED limits, notification permission behavior, SDK_INT_FULL and SDK extensions, stable AIDL version/hash, adb forward --no-rebind tcp:0, Android 11 wireless debugging) are correct. Deductions are for verifiable internal contradictions and stale content: the startup-resolution diagram still labels the UI as Avalonia, Section 8 still describes an Avalonia single-view app with compiled bindings, Section 3 and the groups section give incompatible accounts of the default tools/list surface, the catalog API says no PATCH while the groups section mandates PATCH, the tool_binding_aliases primary key contradicts its stated row semantics, .NET trimming/AOT language survives in the Kotlin runtime description, and the brightness documented-range claim is doubtful. Completeness: all eleven requirements are addressed at contract level, but several load-bearing mechanisms are unspecified rather than merely deferred: how callback implementations are materialized at runtime (abstract classes especially), how IBinder handles for platform AIDL services are acquired without non-SDK APIs, how a roughly 10 GiB catalog reaches app-private storage, how startup resolution is budgeted and reused across boots, who hosts and authenticates the catalog administration HTTP API in the one-APK design, lease renewal and callback.status contracts, table-level storage definitions for callbacks/groups, HIDL reachability, pairing proof-of-possession protocol, and direct-boot receiver behavior. These are concrete design omissions, not implementation gates. Neither score is averaged from prior rounds or from any self-score.
